what: Solana devnet mintTo on the genesis mint
why: Needs a Solana devnet program; the gallery is NEAR sandbox only.
Offline verify.sh tamper is a separate deliverable (scripts/verify.sh --tamper-all), not a contract attack.

what: call a method that changes the stream or payout recipient after open
why: No such method exists in core or market: the recipient is fixed at create_trial / pool open. A04 and M02 attack the only reachable paths and assert the recipient is unchanged.
Core has no platform-withdraw method (launch fee goes to a fixed treasury via permissionless pay_launch_fee). The market has withdraw_platform and M04 attacks it.
Core has no AMM. Sandwich and min_out are market attacks (M06).

what: the real MPC signature on Solana, and Solana-side checks
why: The contract-side F0 policy gate (register_f0_message, sign_genesis, reopen_genesis) is attacked in C02 to C04. The sandbox has no MPC signer, so the signer leg itself and everything on Solana are not attacked here. NEAR cannot see Solana, so confirm_genesis is a signed claim audited by verify.sh (detected, not prevented).

what: launcher against the real token factory (token.primitives.testnet)
why: The sandbox factory is a mock that creates nothing. The real factory runs only on testnet: see evidence/instant-testnet (factory behaviour, registration with 0.00125 NEAR, failed-creation refund).

what: freeze auto-expiry and the 7-day cap timelock by waiting
why: Both are 7 real days even on the demo profile (only the launcher's day unit is 10 s). A sandbox wait would need about 2 million blocks. I36 and I38 assert the bound with the pure kruxa_logic functions and the queued effective_at instead. The core's own FROZEN expiry (D-15) is not a gallery row; tests/tests/negative_paths.rs proves it by rewriting frozen_until in the sandbox state, and A16 asserts the bound with the pure function.
Not in market 1.1.0 (cut first in CO-7); nothing to attack.
